note: Curated references behind the science page and the evidenceCategories on exercises. Summaries describe what the research looked at; they are not treatment claims.

references.title: Breaking up prolonged sitting reduces postprandial glucose and insulin responses
references.summary: Short, regular activity breaks during prolonged sitting were associated with better blood glucose and insulin responses than sitting uninterrupted.

references.title: The sedentary office: an expert statement on the growing case for change towards better health and productivity
references.summary: An expert statement recommending that desk-based workers progressively accumulate more standing and light activity across the workday, and break up prolonged sitting.

references.title: Does physical activity attenuate, or even eliminate, the detrimental association of sitting time with mortality?
references.summary: A large harmonised meta-analysis finding that higher daily physical activity substantially weakened the association between long sitting time and mortality.

references.title: The effects of breaks on low back pain, discomfort, and work productivity in office workers: a systematic review
references.summary: A systematic review of workplace break interventions, finding that active breaks were associated with less discomfort in office workers without reducing productivity.

references.title: Effectiveness of small daily amounts of progressive resistance training for frequent neck/shoulder pain: randomised controlled trial
references.summary: In office workers with frequent neck and shoulder pain, as little as two minutes of daily resistance exercise was associated with reduced pain over ten weeks.

references.title: Effectiveness of exercise in office workers with neck pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis
references.summary: A review of exercise programmes for office workers with neck pain, finding that strengthening and combined exercise were associated with reduced pain and disability.

references.title: Effectiveness of workplace interventions in the prevention of upper extremity musculoskeletal disorders and symptoms: an update of the evidence
references.summary: A systematic review finding moderate evidence that workplace resistance training and combined programmes were associated with fewer upper-limb symptoms.

references.title: "Sit Up Straight": time to re-evaluate
references.source: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy
references.summary: An editorial reviewing evidence that no single sitting posture prevents pain, and that changing position and moving regularly matters more than holding a 'correct' posture.

references.title: How breath-control can change your life: a systematic review on psycho-physiological correlates of slow breathing
references.summary: A systematic review associating slow breathing techniques with increased parasympathetic activity and reports of relaxation and reduced anxiety in healthy adults.

references.title: Digital eye strain: prevalence, measurement and amelioration
references.summary: A review of digital eye strain in screen users, discussing regular breaks from near work, blinking and distance viewing among the practical measures.
